sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2013. Panoan languages and linguistics. Anthropological Papers of the American Museum of Natural History 99. New York: AMNH. (hdl 2246/6448)
sources.note: Nothing on Nawa stress. p. 11 table 1: '*Nawa (of the Môa River) (tentatively classified due to lack of useful linguistic data)'; p. 16 'Nawa is used for a now obsolescent language from the Môa River area in Brazil'; p. 98 (appendix 2) entire documentation = Chandless (1869: 305) 1 word, Rivet & Tastevin (1927-1929/1932) list of 39 verbs, Montagner (2007) 38-word list, 'Note: it cannot be known for certain that these three linguistic sources are for the same language.'

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Nawa language' (Môa Nawa), citing Fleck 2013: 11 and Aguiar 2007 'The Brazilian Panoan languages' (in Wetzels ed., CNWS/ILLA 5: 39-50).

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul & Constant Tastevin. 1927. Les dialectes Pano du haut Juruá et du haut Purus. Anthropos 22: 811-827 (continued in Anthropos 23-24, 1928-1929).
